title: 1 · Tones: the silent last letter
blurb: Read the silent tone letter at the end of a Hmong syllable, name all eight tone spellings, and meet every consonant and vowel of White Hmong.

title: 2 · Letters that sound different: x, s, z, r, c, q, w
blurb: Read the RPA letters that stand for different sounds than in English, and tell plain p, t, k, q from ph, th, kh, qh.

title: 3 · n- and h- sounds: npua, ntawv, hmo, hnub
blurb: Read the nasal starts (np, nt, nk), the breathy hm, hn and hl, the nasal vowels ee and oo, and the vowel pairs.

title: 4 · Nyob zoo, ua tsaug, sib ntsib dua
blurb: Say hello, how are you, thank you, sorry and goodbye the way Hmong Americans do, at any time of day.

title: 5 · kuv, koj, nws, and "the two of us"
blurb: Use the nine Hmong pronouns, including the words for exactly two people.

title: 6 · Two ways to say "is": yog and nyob
blurb: Say what something is with yog, where it is with nyob, and describe with no word for is at all.

title: 7 · puas, los, dab tsi, leej twg, qhov twg
blurb: Ask yes-or-no questions with puas and los tsis yog, and ask what, who, where, when and how many.

title: 8 · tsis and tsis txhob
blurb: Say what you don't know or understand with tsis, answer no, say not yet, and tell someone don't.

title: 9 · Koj lub npe hu li cas?
blurb: Ask and give a name, say where you are from, ask someone's age and clan.

title: 10 · Numbers and money
blurb: Count from one to a million, spell the tens and hundreds right, and talk about dollars.

title: 11 · tus, lub, daim, rab: counting words
blurb: Count people, animals and things with the right counting word: ib tug dev, ob lub tsev, ib phau ntawv.

title: 12 · lub tsheb liab: describing words come after
blurb: Describe things in Hmong order: lub tsheb liab, lub tsev no, kuv lub tsev.

title: 13 · Family: who is speaking?
blurb: Name your family, and choose the word for brother or sister by who is speaking.

title: 14 · Days, times and "when"
blurb: Say when things happen: today, yesterday, tomorrow, the parts of the day, days, months and every day.

title: 15 · Done, doing, going to: lawm, tab tom, yuav
blurb: Show whether an action is done, going on or still to come with lawm, tab tom, yuav and their friends.

title: 16 · pem, nram, tom, tim: up, down, over there
blurb: Say where things are: in, on, at, up there, down there and over there, plus left, right, near and far.

title: 17 · Noj mov: food and eating
blurb: Talk about meals and food, and use noj for eating and haus for drinking.

title: 18 · Verbs in a row: mus yuav, los noj
blurb: String verbs together with no 'and' or 'to': mus yuav zaub, los noj mov, muab … rau.

title: 19 · Please and may I: thov, puas tau
blurb: Ask for help politely, ask permission with puas tau, and tell someone not to do something.

title: 20 · Zoo siab, tu siab, kub, no
blurb: Say how you feel and what the weather is like, with no word for "is".

title: 21 · Pes tsawg? Shopping and prices
blurb: Ask what something costs, say it is expensive or cheap, and buy things with the right counting word.

title: 22 · At the clinic
blurb: Say what hurts, talk to the doctor, take medicine and make an appointment.

title: 23 · More than: tshaj
blurb: Compare two things with tshaj, say "the most", and make words stronger with heev.

title: 24 · Talking with grandparents
blurb: Greet an elder who arrives, ask if they have eaten, see them off, and speak with warmth and respect.

title: 25 · Noj peb caug: Hmong New Year
blurb: Talk about the Hmong New Year: the greeting, the ball toss, the qeej, paj ntaub and new clothes.

title: 26 · Family events and blessings
blurb: Talk about clans, birthdays, family gatherings, soul calling and the wrist-string blessing.
